A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiscoSG work and contain 26 readable pages. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support comparison of the complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v2 reports original parsing experiments, downstream evaluations, and ablations in Tables 3–6, plus annotation-agreement and lexical-diversity results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental and data-analysis results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Generator–Programmer–Interpreter framework, encoder-based deletion, decoder-based insertion, graph-update procedure, training data construction, and losses. The rewritten introductory description introduces no method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DiscoSG-DS and DiscoSG-ED data, Random/Length evaluation scenarios, and DetailCaps, CapArena, and D-FOIL downstream benchmarks. Appendix C retains the same dataset coverage for lexical-diversity analysis.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same 21 parsing baselines, including FACTUAL-T5-base (Sent+Merge), the T5/Qwen variants, GPT-4o variants, GraphRAG, PiVe, Self-Refine, and Prog-Refine. Table 5 retains the same downstream comparator configurations.

E3.justification: Split construction, sample sizes, metrics, model configurations, prompting procedures, and refinement settings remain unchanged. The revised D-FOIL introduction agrees with the reference-generation and human-correction procedure already documented in v2 Section 4.2 and Appendix B.3.

E4.justification: Table 6 retains all analyses of training sources, augmentation scale, refinement depth, edit modalities, and disentangling. The discourse-error analysis, illustrated refinement case, and appendix lexical-diversity analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run information, random-seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Point-estimate and annotation-agreement reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries and illustrated outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains Refiner-base SPICE scores of 64.3/67.3 and teacher scores of 73.1/74.5 on Random/Length. New percentages and ranges summarize existing results; the introduction's loose 'about 30s' timing summary leaves the tabulated 36.9s measurement unchanged.

T1.justification: The probability factorization, graph-update equations, and training objectives in Section 3 are identical, as are the metric definitions in Appendix A.2. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows downstream outperformance from alternative parsers generally to alternative open-source parsers. The task, dataset, refinement contributions, and approximately 30% SPICE and 86× speed claims remain; generalisation is foregrounded but was already claimed in v2 Section 4.1.1.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the higher-capacity-model prescription by explicitly requiring an appropriate architecture and fine-tuning, and more directly links downstream gains to generalisation across graph complexities. These are limited refinements of the existing interpretation; the Limitations section and appendix discussions are unchanged.

D1.justification: The introduction replaces the erroneous description of D-FOIL references as human-written with human-corrected captions checked against a reference. This corrects documentation to match the GPT-4.1 reference-generation process already described in Section 4.2 and Appendix B.3, without establishing a pipeline change. Implementation settings, prompts, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work inventory, Section 5 related-work discussion, and positioning relative to sentence-level parsing and earlier refinement methods remain unchanged. Relocated citations and replacing 'SOTA' with 'strongest' do not introduce a new relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract's second paragraph, several introduction paragraphs, and Section 4.1.1. They reorganize motivation and emphasize graph-complexity generalisation. The overall section structure, method exposition, remaining results discussion, and appendices are retained.

P2.justification: All nine tables and twelve figures retain their content, captions, formatting, and placement. Prose edits change line wrapping within the existing page layout; there is no figure, table, or layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves clarity and internal consistency by narrowing the abstract's comparison scope and removing the incorrect human-written D-FOIL reference description, aligning the introduction with Section 4.2 and Appendix B.3. The generalisation argument is clearer, although some new numerical shorthand is imprecise, such as 'about 30s' versus Table 3's 36.9s. Methods, experimental evidence, and appendix support remain unchanged.
